references.text: It resembles the contrast between hidden actions and revelation in the light, where the one who does evil hates the light and will not come to it, while the one who does truth comes to the light.
Jesus' own response to the accusation of secrecy, where he confirms that he has always spoken openly to the world and has taught nothing in secret.
Jesus' statement that he has not spoken in secret, but everything he said was public, and that he has come as a light for the world.
Describes Jesus' actions in secret (in the wilderness) to avoid capture, illustrating the practical dynamic between secrecy and public danger discussed in the verse.
Refers to Jesus' teaching in the temple (openly) and the remark that no one seized him because his hour had not yet come, reflecting the theme of public action versus hidden schedules.
